paragraphs.text: Personal quality-of-life features for the DeepSeek Harness
# dsh-oliver-qol
Personal quality-of-life features for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh), bundled as one plugin. Each featur
e lives in its own module under `src/features/`, carries its own config section, locale namespace, r
oute prefix, and tests, and never imports another feature.
| Feature | State | What it does |
| `session-delete` | implemented | Permanently deletes a stored session (log, projection cache, work
space accounting, orphaned `.agent-teams` state, task-board execution references) from the session r

ow menu, cascading into its subagent child sessions |
| `extend-settings` | implemented | Adds an **
Extend settings** tab (last) to the settings page; it declares the `settings.extend-settings.item` l

ist slot every QoL setting row registers into |
| `opencode-search` | implemented | The row in that
tab: routes the built-in `web_search` tool through OpenCode Go — endpoint and key reference follow t
he `dsh-opencode-go` plugin settings, while the search model and the proxy address (host + port) are
set in the row itself and touch nothing else. Off by default; while off it delegates to the built-i
n DeepSeek search provider |
## Compatibility
Built against dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`. dsh APIs are pre-stable, so the manifest declares open-ended floors
(`>=0.2.0-rc.2`) instead of pins: a dsh upgrade must not silently drop the bundle, and a real API br
eak surfaces as an error to fix rather than as a plugin that vanished.
## Install
The plugin is a dsh bundle: its `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` (host half) and `dsh.client` (b
a dsh bundle: its `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` (host half) and `dsh.client` (browser half).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Install it as an **npm package**, never as a `github:` dependency. A git install fetches source, so
pnpm rebuilds it on every install, needs a working `pnpm` on `PATH`, needs an `allowBuilds` entry ke
yed by the exact commit URL, and leaves the lockfile pinned to the old commit — enough to make the p
lugin manager report a failure even though the install succeeded. The published package ships `lib/`
, so none of that applies. See docs/DISTRIBUTION.md for the full evidence.
Restart dsh after adding, updating, or removing the plugin. The bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) mo
unts one row (`id: oliver-qol`, `name: dsh-oliver-qol`) and points the web seam's `searchProvider` a
t the `opencode-go` provider this bundle registers.
## Release
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`lib/` is gitignored and built at publish time; it is **not** committed.
## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`sessionDelete.sessionsRoot` must match the `root` of the profile's `session-persistence-jsonl` row
(`$DSH_HOME/sessions` by default). If a deployment moves that root, set both.
`removeOrphanedTeamState` and `pruneTaskBoardReferences` clean the two pieces of state that only *re
ference* a session, after its log is gone. Both are best-effort: a failure is warned and skipped, ne
ver surfaced as a failed delete, because the session the user asked to delete is already deleted.
- **AgentTeams** keeps `<workspace>/.agent-teams/<teamId>/` (`team.json` + member inboxes) under the
directory the session ran in. When the delete removes a team's `captainSessionId`, that team can ne
ver be resumed — the plugin treats the captain as its only owner key — so the directory is removed.
A team that lost only a *member* while its captain lives may still be running or resumable, so it is
**reported, not edited**: rewriting `team.json` from here would race the plugin for a team it still

owns.
- **Task board** keeps `$DSH_HOME/task-board/ledger-v2.json`, and every card's `executions[]`
entry pins the session that performed it. Only those dangling records are dropped. Cards, columns,
prompts, schedules and open executions (`endedAt` absent) are never touched, and an unknown `schemaV
ersion` is refused rather than pattern-matched. The replace is optimistic — the file is re-read imme
diately before the write, and any concurrent change aborts the pass — so losing one cleanup pass is
possible and harmless; clobbering the board's newest state is not.

## Known limitations

- Deletion is permanent; there is no undo. Use archive for reversible hiding.
- A session written by
another dsh process at the same time fails loudly (`session-delete/busy`) on Windows file locks; re

try after that process stops.
- Deleting the currently open session relies on the shipped archive-dr
iven release of the main view; if the client does not release it in time, the request answers `busy`

and can be retried.
- The JSONL storage layout (project directory + encoded session segment) is the
only format coupling; it lives in `src/features/session-delete/jsonl-layout.ts` and `removal.ts` an

d must be re-checked on dsh upgrades.
- The two reference cleanups couple to *other plugins'* on-dis
k layouts, both isolated in their own module and both re-checkable on their plugin's upgrades: `.age
nt-teams/<teamId>/team.json` (`team-state.ts`) and `task-board/ledger-v2.json` schema 6 (`task-board
.ts`). Neither plugin is a dependency — a missing directory, an unknown schema, or an unparsable fil

e leaves the delete behaving exactly as before.
- Task-board pruning is optimistic, not locked: if t
he board writes between the planning read and the replace, that pass is skipped (`changed`) and the

stale references survive until the next delete. There is no retry loop on purpose.
- `opencode-searc
h` delegates to the built-in provider by reading the web service's provider registry (`web.searchPro
viders`) — a dsh-internal surface pinned to the 0.2.0-rc.2 line; re-check it on upgrades. The Extend
-settings row writes the `oliver-qol` profile entry, so renaming the bundle row id makes the row rep

ort `unavailable`.
- `opencode-search` follows the `opencode-go` entry's base `apiKeyEnv` reference
only; multi-account setups (`accounts`/`autoSwitch` in `dsh-opencode-go`) are not followed per searc

h.
- `opencode-search`'s proxy is its own setting: it applies to the search request only. A deployme
nt that wants the search behind the same proxy as chat has to type that address into the new row as

well — there is no "follow the OpenCode Go proxy" mode.
